newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's foreign debt down slightly to $32 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's foreign debt down slightly to $32 bln.

text.p: Nigeria's foreign debt fell to $31.996 billion at the end of June 1996 from $32.581 billion at the end of 1995, the central bank said.

"Total actual external debt service payments during the first half of 1996 amounted to $1.215 billion which represented only 23 percent of the projected annual debt service payment due," the bank said in its half year economic review published on Wednesday.
The report said external assets shot up to $5.174 billion at the end of June 1996 from $3.137 billion at the end of June 1995.
While Nigeria has been servicing its debt to foreign commercial banks regularly it has ignored loans to the Paris club of official creditors who are owed 67 percent of the total debt stock.

The military government is hoping for debt relief and has been talking with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to get their endorsement of its medium-term economic programme so as to secure a rescheduling of repayments.

"An early agreement on a medium-term economic programme being negotiated with the Bretton Woods institutions is critical for resolving the existing external debt overhang, so as to free more resources for growth and development," the central bank report said.
Apart from repayments, Nigeria implements a programme of converting foreign debt to local currency denominated assets.
